title: Stick-On Beginnings
kidRule: UN, DIS and MIS are little beginnings that stick onto the front of a whole word. UN and DIS mean 'not' or 'the opposite', and MIS means 'wrongly'. Never drop or add a letter when you join them: mis + spell = misspell, with both S's.
hint: This word is a little beginning stuck onto a whole word. Spell the beginning, then spell the whole word, and keep every letter from both.
reminder: Just join U-N, D-I-S or M-I-S to the front of the whole word. Do not drop or add any letters.

check.question: Why is UNUSUAL spelled with UN and then the whole word USUAL?
check.correctAnswer: UN just joins onto the front of USUAL, and we keep every letter of both parts!
distractors: Because UN must always be followed by the letter U
Because USUAL loses a letter and UN gives it back

words.def: To have a different idea from someone else.
words.sent: My brother and I disagree about the best ice cream flavor.
words.story: Scientists still disagree about whether Pluto should be called a planet!
words.card: The twins *agree* about pizza but *disagree* about pineapple!

words.def: Not like most others; strange or rare.
words.sent: We saw an unusual purple frog at the zoo.
words.story: The platypus is a very unusual animal: it has fur like a mammal but lays eggs like a bird!
words.card: My *usual* breakfast is toast, but today I got an *unusual* pancake shaped like a moose!

words.story: Most pet cats dislike water, but tigers love to swim!
words.card: I *like* peas, but I *dislike* peas in my shoes!

words.def: Not yet found out or learned about by anyone.
words.sent: The deep ocean is full of unknown creatures.
words.story: Most of the ocean floor has never been mapped in detail, so a lot of our own planet is still unknown!
words.card: I *know* the name of every fish except that *unknown* one wearing a hat!

words.def: To act in a way that breaks the rules.
words.sent: The puppies misbehave when they are bored.
words.story: When a puppy plays too roughly, its brothers and sisters yelp and stop playing, which teaches it to be gentle!
words.card: I *have* three socks that *misbehave* and hide from the washing machine!

words.def: To write a word with the wrong letters.
words.sent: It is easy to misspell a tricky word.
words.story: This word is on many lists of the words that grown-ups get wrong most often, because they forget the second S!
words.card: The wizard cast a *spell* so he would never *misspell* 'abracadabra'!

words.def: To not do what you are told.
words.sent: The puppy did not mean to disobey the rule.
words.story: Guide dogs are taught to disobey on purpose when a command would lead their owner into danger!
words.card: Robots *obey* the rules, but my toaster likes to *disobey*!

words.def: To put something somewhere and then forget where it is.
words.sent: I always misplace my left shoe.
words.story: Squirrels misplace so many of the nuts they bury that some of them grow into new trees!
words.card: Do not *misplace* your shoe*lace* in the spaghetti!

words.def: To go out of sight so that nobody can see you.
words.sent: The rabbit seemed to disappear into the hat.
words.story: An octopus can change its color in less than a second, so it seems to disappear against the rocks!
words.card: Watch the magician make a *pear* *disappear* into his beard!

words.sent: Bringing an umbrella was unnecessary because the sun came out.
words.story: An ostrich's wings may look unnecessary because it cannot fly, but it uses them to steer and balance while it runs!
words.card: A coat is *necessary* in the snow, but a coat on a snowman is *unnecessary*!
